data.title: Margins to remain under pressure for Siemens in near term amid volatility
data.description:
Siemens reported a mixed quarter, with strong revenue, order inflows, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda), and adjusted net profit. But margins have been under pressure due to a combination of commodity inflation and adverse forex movements.
 
The big gains came from Smart Infrastructure (56 per cent of revenue), though all three divisions saw revenue growth. Overall order intake grew 37.8 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y), with government infrastructure investments contributing the most, along with improving private sector capex. But even assuming Smart Infrastructure continues to deliver momentum, margin recovery in the Mobility and Digital Industries segments will be necessary to sustain growth.
 
Management commentary focused on growth in orders and revenue, with policy-driven capex spending across infrastructure being a key driver and improvement in private sector investments being a potential positive. The demand environment remains strong, but commodity inflation and forex volatility are concerns.
 
Order inflows of ₹6,200 crore raised the order book to ₹47,030 crore. Revenue in Q2FY27 grew 17 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹5,730 crore. Gross margin contracted 260 basis points Y-o-Y to 27.3 per cent. This was partially offset by lower-than-expected employee costs as a percentage of sales, while controlled other expenses led to an Ebitda margin beat.
 
Absolute Ebitda increased 3 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹630 crore, but Ebitda margin contracted 150 basis points Y-o-Y to 10.9 per cent. Adjusted net profit increased 4 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹500 crore. Higher other income, up 25.2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹150 crore, was offset by a sharp rise in interest costs, up 200 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹12.6 crore, and an increase in depreciation, up 30 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹89 crore.
 
For H1FY27, revenue increased 16 per cent Y-o-Y on a like-for-like basis to ₹10,400 crore, but Ebitda declined 6 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹1,100 crore. Net profit also declined 6 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹900 crore. The H1FY27 margin contracted 240 basis points Y-o-Y to 10.1 per cent.
 
For H1FY27, operating cash flow (OCF) grew 250 per cent to ₹1,310 crore, and free cash flow (FCF) was ₹1,030 crore (only ₹2 crore in H1FY26). The H1FY27 order inflows were at ₹12,600 crore, up 27 per cent Y-o-Y.
 
Smart Infrastructure has seen strong inflows along with calibrated price hikes over the last six months. Smart Infrastructure revenue increased 20 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3,300 crore, Mobility revenue rose 14 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹1,300 crore, and Digital Industries revenue grew 8 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹1,150 crore.
 
Earnings before interest and tax (Ebit) profitability was pulled down by forex volatility and higher commodity prices. Smart Infrastructure Ebit margin contracted 130 basis points Y-o-Y to 11.7 per cent, Mobility Ebit margin contracted 360 basis points Y-o-Y to 7.5 per cent, and Digital Industries Ebit margin contracted 200 basis points Y-o-Y to 5 per cent.
 
Smart Infrastructure momentum is coming from power utilities, renewables and data centres. Price hikes have helped in quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) margin improvement. Mobility benefited from a robust order book and a ramp-up in locomotive deliveries, factory automation, smart manufacturing and digitalisation across automotive, pharma, chemicals, metals and cement. Digital Industries margin seems to have stabilised at around 5 per cent.
 Apart from commodity inflation and forex volatility, other key risks include a slowdown in order inflows from public infrastructure. Given current macroeconomic conditions, margins could be eroded by overly aggressive bids to win large projects. Related-party transactions with parent group entities at lower valuations are another risk.
 
Consensus opinion for the medium to long term is bullish. The long-term growth prospects will be driven by traction in public capex in areas like transmission and distribution (T&D), metro, railways and utilities, among others. Siemens has a presence across diverse industries due to its expertise in electrification, digitalisation and automation. A focus on localisation and a strong balance sheet are other positive factors.
 
However, it is hard to judge how long the current macroeconomic trends of forex volatility, commodity inflation and fears of supply chain disruptions will remain in force since these are driven by geopolitical tensions. Margin recovery will depend on an easing of those trends. This is where analysts and investors are likely to have differences of opinion.
 
Until there is visibility on an end to the conflict in the Middle East, margin pressures are likely to remain. While more price hikes may be a possibility, these can only compensate with a lag, and some costs would have to be absorbed.
 
The stock is highly valued. There could be a downside, which means conservative investors will wait for changes in the margin profile.

data.title: Discoms not cooperative on EV charging infra, says PM adviser Tarun Kapoor
data.description:
Electricity distribution companies (discoms) are not sufficiently cooperative in setting up electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, and every discom should have a designated officer to address problems faced by charging station operators, said Tarun Kapoor, adviser to the Prime Minister, on Friday.
 
Kapoor, in his speech at a conference organised by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), said electricity distribution companies needed to recognise the growing importance of EVs as a source of power consumption, particularly as India was entering a phase of surplus electricity availability.
 
"Discoms sometimes feel that they make most of their money through industries, so they should concentrate more on that. But this (EVs) again is going to be a very major sector for them and I am quite sure that as we move forward, discoms will realise this and then they will make efforts to ensure that they facilitate charging infrastructure coming up in the country," he said.
  
Kapoor also highlighted the high cost of establishing electricity connections for public charging stations, particularly those requiring higher power capacities of 200 kilowatts (kW) or more. Discoms sometimes demand substantial payments for the electricity infrastructure needed to connect such stations to the grid.
 
"The discoms sometimes are not very cooperative, so we have to ensure that there's some nodal officer in every discom who then can be contacted in case there are issues or in case there are problems," he said.
 
Discoms are largely owned by state governments, although some are privately owned companies operating as licensed electricity distributors. The licences are granted by the respective state electricity regulatory commissions. Improving discoms' cooperation with EV charging operators will require coordination with state governments and electricity regulators.
 
Kapoor, in his speech, said the government had made budgetary provisions under the PM E-DRIVE scheme to cover this cost, adding that a large part of the allocated money remained unspent. The government would also be willing to provide additional funds if required, he said.
 
Another challenge is the low utilisation of existing public charging stations, which is affecting their maintenance. Kapoor said oil marketing companies had reported utilisation of less than 1 per cent at some locations.
 
"Earlier also, some charging stations were installed in various public locations and gradually, due to disuse, they were not maintained and then they became almost useless," he said.
 
He said the government was looking beyond petrol pumps to expand charging infrastructure, with housing societies, office complexes and public parking lots among the possible locations. Charging stations should be installed where vehicles are generally parked for longer periods, he said.
 
Kapoor also called for greater use of daytime charging to utilise surplus electricity, particularly solar power. He said India often had surplus electricity during the day, while demand pressures were higher during peak hours. Installing chargers at workplaces could encourage people to charge their vehicles during the day.
 
Kapoor said electric truck manufacturers should avoid developing exclusive charging networks for their respective vehicles. He said charging stations along highways should be accessible to vehicles made by different manufacturers so that infrastructure gets sufficient users and remains properly maintained.
 
The government also wants charging infrastructure for electric buses, trucks and heavy vehicles used in mining and industrial applications. Kapoor said bus depots could be opened up for use by other EVs, and the government was asking state governments to facilitate this.
 
SIAM President Shenu Agarwal, in his speech at the conference, said the automobile industry, electricity distribution companies, oil marketing companies, charging operators and state governments needed to work together to expand the network.
 
"Automakers bring vehicle and charger compatibility, oil marketing companies bring prime land and retail reach, charge point operators bring technology and service, discoms bring grid access and states bring approvals, land and demand implications," Agarwal said.
 
He described electric truck charging as the next frontier, adding that bus depots and freight corridors would require high-power charging facilities. SIAM members were keen to work with energy and infrastructure partners to develop this network, he said.

data.title: Canada PR wait falls for parents, rises for Express Entry applicants
data.description:
Canada has reduced waiting times for permanent residence (PR) applications in several categories, including provincial nominee and parents’ sponsorship programmes, according to the latest data released by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) on November 17.
 
However, not all applicants have seen shorter waits. Processing times for skilled workers applying through the Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP) have increased by two months, while those sponsoring their spouses are also facing longer waits.
 
The Canadian Experience Class (CEC) processing time remained unchanged at six months, while applicants under the base Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) saw waiting times fall by one month to 12 months. The Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP) recorded a reduction of two months for applicants outside Quebec and three months for those intending to settle in the province.
  
For applicants already in Canada who are waiting for a decision on their PR applications, a Bridging Open Work Permit (BOWP) may allow them to continue working. Those who apply before their existing work permit expires may benefit from maintained status, allowing them to work under the same conditions while their application is being processed.
 
Canada PR processing times: Economic immigration
 
Waiting times across most economic immigration programmes either fell or remained unchanged. The Federal Skilled Worker Program was the main exception, with processing times increasing by two months.
 
Express Entry
 
Processing times for the FSWP increased from seven months to nine months. The number of pending applications also rose by 1,800 to 60,100.
 
The Canadian Experience Class (CEC), meanwhile, continued to have a six-month processing time, even as its pending applications fell by 5,700 to 48,200.
 
Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Canadian Experience Class (CEC): 6 months; unchanged.
Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP): 9 months; up from 7 months.
Federal Skilled Trades Program (FSTP): Not available in both updates.
 
Service standard: Six months for all Express Entry programmes.
 
Applications awaiting assessment:
 
CEC: 48,200, down 5,700.
FSWP: 60,100, up 1,800.
 
Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)
 
Applicants under the base PNP category saw processing times fall by one month to 12 months. The number of pending applications also declined by 6,300 to 90,200.
 
For applicants applying through the Express Entry-linked enhanced PNP stream, the waiting period remained unchanged at seven months. Its pending applications increased by 700 to 13,800.
 
Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Enhanced PNP (through Express Entry): 7 months; unchanged.
Base PNP (through non-Express Entry): 12 months; down from 13 months.
 
Service standards: Six months for enhanced PNP applications and 11 months for base PNP applications.
 
Applications awaiting assessment:
 
Enhanced PNP: 13,800, up 700.
Base PNP: 90,200, down 6,300.
 
Under a temporary federal measure introduced on June 9, 2026, eligible PNP applicants can apply for a BOWP without waiting to receive an Acknowledgement of Receipt (AOR) for their PR application.
 
Quebec immigration
 
Processing times for the Quebec Business Class (QBC) fell by two months to 73 months. The Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ), however, remained unchanged at 11 months.
 
The number of pending PSTQ applications declined by 400 to 20,100, while the QBC inventory remained unchanged at 3,600.
 
Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ): 11 months; unchanged.
Quebec Business Class (QBC): 73 months; down from 75 months.
 
Service standards: Six months for PSTQ applicants. No service standard is published for QBC applications.
 
Applications awaiting assessment:
 
PSTQ: 20,100, down 400.
QBC: 3,600, unchanged.
 
Atlantic Immigration Program
 
Processing times under the Atlantic Immigration Program (AIP) fell by one month to 25 months. The number of applications awaiting assessment also declined by 400 to 11,100.
 
Processing time (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Atlantic Immigration Program: 25 months, down from 26 months.
 
Service standard: 11 months.
 
Applications awaiting assessment: 11,100, down 400.
 
Other economic immigration programmes
 
Applicants under the Start-Up Visa (SUV) and Federal Self-Employed Persons Program (FSEPP) continued to face estimated waiting times of more than 10 years.
 
The SUV inventory fell marginally by 100 applications to 47,400, while the FSEPP backlog remained unchanged at 8,000.
 
Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Start-Up Visa (SUV): More than 10 years; unchanged.
Federal Self-Employed Persons Program (FSEPP): More than 10 years; unchanged.
 
Service standards: Not available for these programmes.
 
Applications awaiting assessment:
 
SUV: 47,400, down 100.
FSEPP: 8,000, unchanged.
 
Canada PR processing times: Family sponsorship
 
Family sponsorship applicants saw mixed changes in the latest update. Waiting times for spouses and common-law partners increased by one month across all categories, while the Parents and Grandparents Program recorded shorter waiting periods.
 
Sponsorship outside Quebec
 
Processing times for sponsoring a spouse or common-law partner increased by one month, whether the partner was living in Canada or abroad.
 
In contrast, the waiting period under the PGP fell by two months to 26 months. The number of applications awaiting assessment under this programme also declined by 1,800 to 33,800.
 
Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Spouse or common-law partner living in Canada: 27 months, up from 26 months.
Spouse or common-law partner living outside Canada: 19 months, up from 18 months.
Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP): 26 months, down from 28 months.
 
Service standard: 12 months for sponsoring a spouse or common-law partner outside Quebec. No service standards are published for the other categories.
 
Applications awaiting assessment:
 
Partner living in Canada: 55,100, down 500.
Partner living outside Canada: 65,900, up 300.
Parents and Grandparents: 33,800, down 1,800.
 
Sponsorship within Quebec
 
Applicants sponsoring spouses or common-law partners who intend to settle in Quebec also faced a one-month increase in processing times.
 
The PGP recorded a three-month reduction, with the estimated waiting period falling to 60 months.
 
Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Spouse or common-law partner living in Canada: 33 months, up from 32 months.
Spouse or common-law partner living outside Canada: 34 months, up from 33 months.
Parents and Grandparents Program: 60 months, down from 63 months.
 
Service standards: IRCC does not publish service standards for family sponsorship applications involving applicants intending to settle in Quebec.
 
Applications awaiting assessment:
 
Partner living in Canada: 14,700, up 200.
Partner living outside Canada: 19,700, up 300.
Parents and Grandparents: 10,100, down 200.
 
Canada citizenship processing times
 
Processing times for most citizenship-related applications remained unchanged in the November update.
 
The waiting period for a citizenship grant remained at 12 months, in line with IRCC's service standard. Applications for renunciation of citizenship continued to take four months.
 
The processing time for searches of citizenship records improved by one month to 18 months.
 
Processing times (November 17; previous update: October 9):
 
Citizenship grant: 12 months; unchanged.
Renunciation of citizenship: 4 months; unchanged.
Search of citizenship records: 18 months, down from 19 months.
 
Service standard: 12 months for citizenship grants.
 
IRCC reported 322,900 citizenship grant applications in its November update, an increase of 200 from October 9.

data.title: Industry body GJC alerts BIS over gold adulteration using Rhenium, Iridium
data.description:
The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) on Friday said it alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) about reports of the alleged use of Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys to increase gold's weight, and urged the industry and consumers to remain vigilant.

"While there have been media reports from certain quarters regarding the possible misuse of materials such as Rhenium and Iridium in gold, we want to assure the entire jewellery industry and all gold buyers that there is absolutely no reason to panic. The Bureau of Indian Standards is treating the matter with utmost seriousness," GJC Chairman Rajesh Rokde said in a statement.

 

According to media reports, Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys were allegedly used to increase gold's weight without a corresponding increase in purity.

GJC appealed to all jewellers and consumers to immediately report any instance of suspected adulteration, fraudulent activity or malpractice.

"Such complaints can be lodged with GJC as well as directly with the Bureau of Indian Standards, enabling prompt investigation and necessary action," Rokde said.

He said every jeweller must undertake stringent quality control checks of gold procured from manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers and keep consumer service as the top priority.

He advised buyers not to fall prey to lower making charge offers and to purchase gold only from trusted retailers.

Consumers should also verify hallmark details through the BIS Care App and insist on GST-paid invoices, said Rokde.

"We remain committed to protecting the interests of both the industry and consumers. Any proven case of adulteration or malpractice will be strongly pursued with the appropriate authorities, and strict action should be taken against anyone found manufacturing, supplying or using such materials for fraudulent purposes," he said.

GJC Vice Chairman Avinash Gupta said isolated reports or rumours should not be allowed to undermine consumer confidence in the gems and jewellery sector.

"We encourage all jewellers to strengthen internal quality control processes and ensure complete compliance and transparency with BIS hallmarking regulations. Consumers, on their part, should purchase jewellery only from reputable jewellers, obtain proper invoices and verify hallmark credentials before making a purchase," he added.

data.title: Machine tool makers seek ₹3,000 crore fund to cut dependence on imports
data.description:
The Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers’ Association (IMTMA) has sought a ₹3,000-crore government-backed fund to acquire 25-30 advanced manufacturing technologies from Europe and the United States, aiming to reduce the country’s dependence on imported machine tools by ₹8,000-10,000 crore.
 
The proposal is part of the industry’s recommendations for the Union Budget 2027-28, which the association plans to raise with the Secretary of the Ministry of Heavy Industries on Saturday.
 
The proposed Machine Tool Technology Acquisition Fund would comprise ₹1,000 crore in grants, ₹1,000 crore in soft loans and another ₹1,000 crore for equity co-investment by the government in strategic transactions, according to the association’s detailed note on Budget demands.
  
The association said India continues to import 60 per cent of its metalworking machine tools by value, with high-end technologies concentrated in Europe and the US. It argued that high interest rates in India make overseas technology acquisitions prohibitively expensive for domestic manufacturers.
 
The industry demands come at a time when domestic consumption of machine tools has outpaced domestic production. This “widening gap between demand and supply is being filled by rising imports,” said Mohini Kelkar, president of IMTMA. According to the association, the value of machine tool production increased by 19 per cent year-on-year to ₹17,387 crore in FY26, against a 15 per cent rise in domestic consumption to ₹36,419 crore. Imports, meanwhile, grew 16 per cent year-on-year to ₹21,628 crore during the same period. “China accounts for almost 25 per cent of such imports,” Kelkar said, adding that a lack of technology is the biggest impediment to domestic production.
 
The association has also sought a separate ₹1,000-crore technology upgradation fund to help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It has proposed an interest subsidy of 5-6 per cent, with assistance capped at ₹200 crore per enterprise, a loan tenure of seven to 10 years and a two-year moratorium.
 
IMTMA said Indian machine tool MSMEs currently pay interest rates of around 7-10 per cent on loans for technology upgradation, compared with subsidised rates of 1-4 per cent in China, 2-4 per cent in South Korea and 1-3 per cent in Taiwan.
 
Separately, the association has called for a dedicated production-linked incentive (PLI)-like scheme to promote the indigenisation of core machine tool technologies. The industry has sought a requirement for companies benefiting from PLI schemes to source at least 60 per cent of their overall capital goods procurement from domestic manufacturers.
 
IMTMA has also proposed setting up a National Mission for Core Technologies, jointly anchored by a national research and development institution, academia and the machine tool industry.
 
On the trade policy front, the association has sought an additional 2 per cent basic customs duty on imports under the broad ‘Others’ classification of machinery and mechanical appliances under HS Code 84798999. It said imports under this category stood at $2.19 billion in 2025-26, arguing that the classification could be used to import machinery without adequate product-specific identification. The proposed duty would apply even to imports under free and preferential trade agreements.
 
The industry has also sought access to granular, machine-wise import data to identify the types, specifications and sources of imported machinery, including a distinction between new and second-hand equipment. It has urged the government to reconsider Section 135AA of the Customs Act, which it says has restricted access to such information, or alternatively allow relevant ministries to access the data for policy planning and import substitution.
 
The association has further sought discontinuation of the Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) scheme, or its restriction to machinery that is not manufactured domestically. It argued that zero-duty imports under the scheme create a cost disadvantage for Indian capital goods manufacturers, which pay duties on imported components and taxes on domestic procurement.

data.title: Rail link, trading post, infra projects on anvil during Nepal PM visit
data.description:
During Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s two-day visit to New Delhi, which begins on Sunday, India is likely to announce a substantial economic package for its northern neighbour. Agreements are also slated to be inked between the two sides on investments in Nepal's education, health and hydropower sectors and to increase connectivity, including reciprocal overflight access.
 
A $2 billion development package from India, some of which will help with reconstruction projects in Nepal following the glacial floods in August, is being discussed. Sources said the two sides are still giving final shape to the package. If finalised, it will be the largest such one-time package that India has given to any of its neighbours. The glacial flood in Nepal left over 1,500 people dead, with over 5,200 still missing, and damaged over 7,000 homes and several hydroelectric projects.
 
 
A cross-border weekly train service connecting Nepal’s Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantonment will be flagged off, and an integrated check post in the border town of Banbasa in Uttarakhand’s Champawat district, 50 km from Uttar Pradesh’s Pilibhit district, will be inaugurated.
 
The Nepal PM will land in New Delhi on Sunday afternoon and hold delegation-level talks with Modi on Monday, leaving for Kathmandu a little after that. This will be Shah’s first bilateral visit not just to India but outside Nepal since forming his government after his party, the Rastriya Swatantra Party, won a landslide in the general elections. He travelled to New York in September to address the United Nations General Assembly.
 
Modi and Shah will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement it issued on Friday afternoon. It said India-Nepal bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress in trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports.
 
In Kathmandu on Friday, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said a 34-member delegation comprising Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Minister of Foreign Affairs Shisir Khanal and others will accompany Shah to New Delhi. Wagle was in India for a three-day visit in September and also visited in October, while India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri was in Kathmandu earlier this month. Both India and Nepal have appointed new ambassadors to each other’s capitals. A 52-member business delegation from Nepal will also be in India during the Nepal PM’s visit to New Delhi, and a Nepal-India Business Forum is slated to meet.

data.title: Polycab India faces near-term volume, margin pressure as metal prices fall
data.description:
The stock of the country’s largest cables and wires (C&W) company, Polycab India, has slipped about 8 per cent over the past week on worries that inventory losses, price cuts and increased competitive pressures will weigh on its near-term outlook. While the company delivered a strong September quarter performance, short-term headwinds, a higher year-ago base and peaking growth concerns are likely to lead to growth moderation going ahead. After a strong growth trend over the last four years, Polycab may underperform peers going ahead. At the current price (₹7,575), the stock is trading at about 30 times its FY28 earnings estimates.
 
The sharp correction in copper and aluminium prices and subsequent inventory losses are expected to weigh on the company and the sector.
 
Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange have declined by 11-12 per cent from September highs of $14,870 per metric tonne, while aluminium prices have retreated to levels last seen in January 2026. Current spot prices are down 9 per cent for aluminium and 4 per cent for copper, and these are below their respective Q2FY27 averages.
 
The 21 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) increase in copper prices in Q3FY26 had prompted distributors to advance purchases ahead of further price hikes. This resulted in unusually strong volume growth during the quarter, with Polycab India registering 40 per cent growth, RR Kabel gaining 30 per cent in the domestic market and Finolex Cables rising 28 per cent in the wires business. With metal prices now easing, Nishant Bagrecha and Rohan Kalle of InCred Research believe that distributors could delay replenishment in anticipation of lower procurement costs. If the downtrend persists, channel stocking is likely to remain subdued in Q3FY27, creating a tougher volume growth comparison for C&W companies. The brokerage has an 'add' rating on Polycab with a target price of ₹9,800.
 
Given the disruption in prices and competitive pressures, brokerages expect margins to come under pressure. Overall operating profit margins in the September quarter for Polycab were down 139 basis points year-on-year (Y-o-Y), while they improved by 53 basis points on a sequential basis. While margins in the core C&W segment were at 14.2 per cent, profitability in the fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) segment stood at its highest level of 10.1 per cent. The financial health of the FMEG segment has been improving, and the business reported its seventh consecutive profitable quarter. While there is price volatility, once commodity prices stabilise, margins are expected to recover given a volume uptick and operating leverage.
 
Motilal Oswal Research also points out that the C&W sector is entering a more challenging phase amid several headwinds, such as a sharp correction in copper and aluminium prices, which typically triggers inventory losses, as well as faster price pass-through and channel destocking. The other risks, according to the brokerage, are the increase in competitive intensity with the entry of UltraTech Cement with its Ultravolt brand and uncertainty around global AI/data centre-led infrastructure spending.
 
Growth momentum for the sector is expected to moderate in the near term due to the recent softness in commodity prices. This follows a strong 18 per cent value growth delivered by organised players over the FY22-26 period.
 
Sanjeev Kumar Singh and Mudit Agarwal of the brokerage point out that multiple headwinds led the Polycab stock to derate from its peak valuation of 40-42 times price-to-earnings on a one-year forward basis to about 30 times.
 
They, however, maintain a 'buy' rating on the stock with a target price of ₹10,000. Their buy call is based on its leadership position in the C&W industry and a strong balance sheet, which supports business operations during such volatile market conditions.

data.title: Strand eyes US, Southeast Asia mkts for blood-based cancer screening test
data.description:
Strand Life Sciences, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries, is looking to expand its blood-based cancer screening test, CancerSpot, into overseas markets, with the US, Southeast Asia and the Middle East among the regions it is targeting.
 
The company is pursuing US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for the test and expects the regulatory process to reach a key milestone around February-March next year. The US would be its next export market once approval comes through, a company representative said.
 
“In most regions of the world, one doesn't (require regulatory approval to operate). Our aspiration is global. There is good opportunity in Southeast Asia, in the Middle East and in other parts of the world, which we will be aggressively pursuing,” Dr Ramesh Hariharan, chief executive officer of Strand Life Sciences, said.
 
 
Regulatory requirements vary across markets, and the company will pursue approvals wherever they are required. Hariharan said such clearances also help build confidence among clinicians and other stakeholders.
 
CancerSpot uses genome sequencing, DNA methylation analysis and artificial intelligence (AI) to identify patterns in DNA fragments circulating in the blood that may be associated with cancer. The test has demonstrated the ability to screen for 14 types of cancer.
 
The company is also looking to make the test more affordable in India. It is currently priced at up to ₹25,000 for patients, with Strand targeting a price of less than ₹10,000 over the next few years.
 
The longer-term ambition is to bring the cost down further and make the test part of routine preventive health checks. However, the company has not specified a timeline for reaching that price point.
 
Reducing costs will depend on improvements in sequencing technology, procurement and laboratory processes, as well as higher volumes. Strand said its sequencing equipment is shared with its wider genomics testing operations, while sample collection, assay development and research account for a significant part of the costs.
 
The company is also working to build awareness among doctors and patients as it looks to scale up the service. It is in discussions with hospitals and academic institutions on collaborations, including larger clinical studies. Hospitals are important to the process because a positive screening result needs follow-up investigations and clinical care.
 
CancerSpot is a screening test and does not provide a definitive cancer diagnosis. A positive result needs to be followed by targeted imaging or endoscopy and, where indicated, a biopsy to confirm the presence of cancer.
 
The company’s four-year study, conducted across 43 hospitals in India and involving around 1,400 participants, included about 950 people with cancer and 450 healthy individuals. In an independent set of participants, the test recorded a false-positive rate of 1.4 per cent. The study reported that it detected 72 per cent of cancers, including around 65-70 per cent at early stages.
 
Strand said the test is intended to complement, rather than replace, established screening methods such as mammography and colonoscopy. It covers several cancer types for which routine screening options are limited or unavailable.

data.title: OTT releases this week: List of new OTTs to watch on various platforms
data.description:
Are you searching for a new OTT series for your weekend watch? This week has seen a variety of films and web series debut on OTT platforms, showcasing a blend of genres including comedy, romance, drama, thrillers, and action. 
 
Highlighted by the highly anticipated film The Odyssey from Christopher Nolan and the return of the beloved comedy series Dhindora featuring Bhuvan Bam in its second season, there is a lot to consider for your watchlist. 
 
Numerous streaming services like Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, JioHotstar, ZEE5, and more have introduced new releases in different languages and categories. Here’s an overview of the films and series available for streaming this week.
 

Best OTT releases this week to watch 

1. The Odyssey (Prime Video, Apple TV)
 
Christopher Nolan's grand interpretation of the Greek poem by Homer centers on Odysseus, portrayed by Matt Damon, as he navigates his challenging path back to his homeland after the fall of Troy The movie is set to debut on November 17, 2026.
 
2. Dhindora Season 2 (Netflix)
 
Well-known comic series Dhindora, featuring Bhuvan Bam, returns for its second season. This time, the romantic journey of Titu Mama is in focus. Dhindora 2 is set to debut on Netflix on November 20, 2026, moving away from YouTube for this new season.

The college series returns with its second season, reuniting 6 friends as they journey through another stage of existence at Excel University. data.title: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao briefly turns billionaire after blockbuster IPO
data.description:
Krishna Rao, the chief financial officer of Anthropic, briefly became a billionaire following the blockbuster debut of the frontier AI model company’s shares on Thursday.
 
Rao, who is of Indian origin, holds 94.97 million shares of Anthropic and did not sell any shares in the public offering.
 
Anthropic's shares opened at $111.50 and hit an intraday high of $115.10, valuing Rao's holding at about $1.1 billion. The stock later pared gains to close at $97.17 on the New York Stock Exchange. His holding is now worth $923 million.
 
It is unusual for a company’s CFO to become a billionaire following the company's IPO, but Rao is one of those key personnel, along with hundreds of Anthropic employees who have now become millionaires because of their stock holdings in a company that was set up just five years ago.
 
 
“Before I joined Anthropic, Tom Brown took me on a long walk around San Francisco. We covered a lot of ground that day, and spent a couple hours talking about where the models and the compute behind them were headed. I will admit that parts of it sounded like science fiction, but I found myself replaying our conversation in my head for the rest of the afternoon. I remember getting home later that night and thinking that if even 10% of it came true, it would change the way we live and work,” he wrote on LinkedIn.
 
The 43-year-old, Anthropic’s first CFO, is known to be a straight talker and has largely stayed out of the limelight while the spotlight remained on the seven co-founders, including Dario and Daniela Amodei. He has been instrumental in helping the company raise billions of dollars in funding over the last two years.
 
Rao has been with Anthropic since 2024, when the company was still considered an underdog to OpenAI. Before that, he was the CFO of Fanatics Commerce, an online sports merchandise and retail platform, and had also previously worked with Airbnb. He began his career as a strategy consultant at Bain, a global management consulting firm, from September 2005 to July 2008. He holds a JD from Yale Law School and an AB in economics from Harvard College.
